primaryText: Mary had to take the train to go to Paris.

readings.name: root: given Mary's circumstances then, a past necessity to take the train then
root evaluated now: given her circumstances now, a necessity to have taken the train then

comment: A root modal is evaluated at the time tense provides.

primaryText: Mary had to be home (at the time of the crime).
context: Evidence gathered a week ago pointed to Mary being home at the time of the murder; yesterday Poirot debunked her alibi.

readings.name: epistemic over past: given what is known now, it is necessary that Mary was home
past over epistemic: given what was known then, it was necessary that Mary was home

comment: False in the scenario: an epistemic cannot describe a past epistemic state without an attitude, indirect discourse, or an overt background.

primaryText: Two days ago, Poirot thought that Mary had to be home.
context: Evidence gathered a week ago pointed to Mary being home at the time of the murder; yesterday Poirot debunked her alibi.
comment: The modal's time of evaluation is Poirot's thinking time; the past morpheme is sequence of tense.

primaryText: This didn't make sense, thought Poirot... Mary had to be home.
context: Evidence gathered a week ago pointed to Mary being home at the time of the murder; yesterday Poirot debunked her alibi.
comment: An indirect discourse past tense.

primaryText: Given what Poirot knew then, Mary had to be home.
context: Evidence gathered a week ago pointed to Mary being home at the time of the murder; yesterday Poirot debunked her alibi.
comment: An overt conversational background performs the event anchoring itself.

primaryText: Gianni può aver parlato a Maria.
translation: Gianni may have talked to Maria.

readings.name: epistemic
deontic or ability

comment: The complement is backshifted with respect to the modal: only the epistemic reading.

primaryText: Gianni ha potuto parlare a Maria.
translation: Gianni was able to talk to Maria.

readings.name: deontic or ability
epistemic

comment: Tense and aspect morphology on the modal put it in the scope of tense: no epistemic reading.

primaryText: Mary put soulever cette table, mais elle ne la souleva pas.
translation: Mary was able to lift this table, but she didn't lift it.
comment: The continuation contradicts the actuality entailment of the perfective root modal.

primaryText: John put prendre le train, bien qu'il soit possible qu'il ne l'ait pas pris.
translation: John may have taken the train, even though it's possible he didn't.

readings.name: epistemic
root: John managed to take the train, but it is possible he didn't

comment: No contradiction on the epistemic reading: tense and aspect are interpreted below the modal.

primaryText: Mary put prendre le train.
translation: Mary may have taken the train / was able to take the train.

readings.name: epistemic over aspect: some world compatible with what is known holds a past train-taking by Mary
aspect over root: an actual past event which in some circumstantial world is a train-taking by Mary

comment: (18) and (19): the two LFs; only the second forces the event into the actual world.

primaryText: Mary had to take the train.

readings.name: given Mary's circumstances then, she had to take the train then
given Mary's circumstances now, she had to take the train

comment: Relativized to the subject, the modal is keyed to the time tense gives.

primaryText: Mary had to be home.

readings.name: given what I know now, it must be the case that Mary was home then
given what I knew then, Mary had to be home

comment: Relativized to the speaker, the modal is keyed to the speech time.

primaryText: John thought that Mary might be home.

readings.name: given what John knew at his thinking time, it was possible Mary was home
given what John knows now, it was possible Mary was home

comment: Relativized to the attitude holder, the modal is keyed to the attitude time.

primaryText: John thought yesterday that Mary had taken the train the day before.
comment: Three events: the speech event, John's thinking yesterday, and Mary's train-taking the day before.

primaryText: John might have thought yesterday that Mary had taken the train the day before.

readings.name: speech event: given what I know now, it is possible that John thought Mary had taken the train

primaryText: John thought yesterday that Mary might have taken the train the day before.

readings.name: attitude event: given what John thought yesterday, it was possible that Mary had taken the train
speech event: John thought yesterday that it was possible, given what I know, that Mary took the train

comment: The modal must be keyed to the closest event.

primaryText: John thought yesterday that Mary had to take the train the day before.

readings.name: VP event: given Mary's circumstances the day before yesterday, it was necessary that she take the train
speech event: John thought that it was necessary given what I know that Mary took the train

primaryText: John is the murderer.
comment: True in all of the speaker's doxastic alternatives, the content of the asserting event.

primaryText: John believes it might be raining.

readings.name: rain is compatible with what John believes

comment: The epistemic quantifies directly over the worlds the attitude provides, avoiding the problem of introspection.

primaryText: It must be raining.
comment: In all worlds compatible with the content of the speech event it is raining; the ordering source makes it weaker than the bare assertion.

primaryText: Suppose that it is raining and that it might not be raining.
comment: Lack of rain cannot be compatible with one's suppositions if one already supposes that it is raining.

primaryText: Last night Mary had to take the train to go to Paris.

readings.name: epistemic for the subject: it was necessary, last night, given what Mary knew, that she took the train

comment: Anchored to the VP event, which has no content, the modal cannot be epistemic.

primaryText: John konnte sehen/merken, dass Mary nett war.
translation: John could see/notice that Mary was nice.

readings.name: epistemic for the subject: Mary being nice was compatible with what John came to know

comment: The complement is an attitude event with content, so the low modal can be epistemic. Credited to I. Heim.

primaryText: John a pu voir/remarquer que Mary était gentille.
translation: John could see/notice that Mary was nice.

readings.name: epistemic for the subject: Mary being nice was compatible with what John came to know

comment: The low position is shown by the actuality entailment.

primaryText: Last night Mary had to take the train to go to Paris.
comment: Obligatorily circumstantial: the circumstances of the train-taking, Mary's need to go to Paris, her car breaking down, the timetable.

primaryText: A lot of people can jump in this pool.
comment: A circumstantial reading with no agentive subject: the circumstances highlight properties of the location. Credited to Hackl (1998).
